marta: Quick compliance ping 1 we're evaluating Asterion-9B-emb for our embeddings product (small, fast). License snippet below - question: can we offer embedding vectors via hosted API (customers pay) if we apply product quantization / dimensionality reduction?

ash quick note: embedding pipeline: FP32 1536 -> PQ (16x16) producing 256-dim codes + codebooks stored server-side. We never ship codebooks or raw FP32 to customers, only compressed vectors via API.

marta: pasted license excerpt from upstream model repo: 

oncall-bot: ```
Asterion Academic Research License v0.9
- For noncommercial research and educational use only.
- Redistribution of model weights or derivatives (including quantized binaries) is prohibited without express permission.
- Derivative works must be made available under the same license (share-alike).
- Hosting a service that provides model outputs to paying users is a commercial activity and is not permitted without a commercial license.
```

dinesh: engineering POV 1 - technically PQ codes + codebooks are a compressed representation; the codebook is necessary to reconstruct float vectors. Are compressed codes considered "derivatives"? if yes, shipping them (or letting customers download) probably triggers redistrib clause.

sam (legal): high-level: two issues: 1) commercial hosting prohibition likely blocks providing a paid embeddings API; 2) share-alike clause may require us to release modifications (unclear how it applies to post-processing like PQ or PCA). We need to interpret whether a transformation that reduces dimensionality is a "derivative" or a "tooling transform." Usually license drafters treat weight transformations as derivatives.

josh: product question: many enterprise customers ask for lower-dim embeddings for storage and speed. If we can't provide hosted low-dim vectors, can we offer a pattern where the customer runs a conversion step on their side (BYO transform) or we provide code (not weights) for conversion?

dinesh: feasible: option A - provide transformation code only (numpy/PyTorch) and customers run locally (BYO model) -> complies with license but worse UX. Option B - keep hosted API but only serve original embeddings and let customers do offline reduction. Option C - ask upstream for a commercial embed license or an exception that PQ codebooks are allowed.

sam (legal): recommended steps: 1) don't enable paid hosting for Asterion until we get a commercial license/waiver; 2) don't distribute codebooks or quantized weights externally; 3) determine whether providing compressed vectors via API is "redistribution" 1 - likely yes if they can be used to reconstruct model behavior. We'll draft an outreach clarifying these specifics and request a hosting carve-out and a permissive redistribution clause for compressed embeddings.

oncall-bot: policy reminder: mark onboarding sheet field "legal" = pending and set "hosted:blocked" flag.

marta: action plan: (a) dinesh attach precise PQ pipeline + whether codebook keys reveal model internals; (b) sam + legal draft email asking for (i) permission to host embeddings for paying customers, (ii) permission to store/distribute compressed vectors (PQ codes) and/or (iii) permission to provide conversion code under MIT; (c) josh prepare customer messaging fallback (BYO transform doc).

dinesh: added perf numbers: original 1536-dim (fp32) recall@10 = 0.732; PQ-256 recall@10 = 0.714 (-2.5%); storage drop x6. Latency improved 3x. I'll attach the bench csv to the onboarding folder.

sam (legal): note for outreach: include exact license file and hash, explain we will not publish compressed binaries publicly unless permitted, propose attribution text and a short SLA limitation. We'll aim to send to Asterion upstream by EOD Thu.

marta: thanks. keeping thread open. if anyone sees an urgent sales ask, escalate to me and we'll use the BYO pattern as a stopgap. :pray:
